definition: holding the cost of care on our own assets rather than buying a policy for it

settled:
We buy no long-term care cover, and carrying it on our own assets is the plan rather than the absence of one.

I am forty and Jen is thirty-seven, so nothing here is likely to matter for twenty years or more, and about one point seven million or more compounding across that gap will probably keep beating what a carrier would sell us.

I will re-run the sum at fifty-five to sixty. Until then the action is the review, not the purchase.

title: Carrying The Long Term Care Risk Myself
